# commutator subgroup　`def.commutator-subgroup`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.commutator-subgroup)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.commutator-subgroup.md)

⭐ Relation to solvability: set $G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(i+1)} = [G^{(i)}, G^{(i)}]$ (the **derived series**). Then $G$ is solvable if and only if some $G^{(i)} = \{e\}$.

⚠ This differs from the **lower central series** $\gamma_{i+1} = [G, \gamma_i]$: the derived series commutators each term with itself, while the lower central series only commutators with $G$; termination of the lower central series gives nilpotence, which is stronger than solvability.

> Proofs of the edges are still Chinese only: `proofs/`; the Chinese page remains authoritative.
